name: Helix Foundry
cost: Free (Apache 2.0) to run yourself. The README doesn't state pricing for the hosted version
works_with: Claude, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock or any OpenAI-compatible server
short: Connect your company's databases, apps and documents, let an agent draft an ontology, then explore it as one graph you can ask questions of.
what: Foundry connects PostgreSQL, MySQL, Amazon S3, Stripe, PostHog, WorkOS, GitHub, Linear, Granola and Cal.com, and takes uploaded documents and table files. An agent drafts an ontology: types, links, where each one comes from, and rules. You review and edit it, then load it into HelixDB. You can explore the result as a graph or as records, trace every value back to its row or quote, and ask questions that come back with cited answers.
who: Teams whose data is spread across databases and SaaS tools and who want one connected view they can question. You run it with Docker, so skip it if you'd rather not, or use the hosted version.
needs: For AI: an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the shell you start it from, or Ollama or LM Studio on your computer

steps.title: Clone and start it
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/helixdb/helix-foundry.git
cd helix-foundry
docker compose up -d --wait

steps.title: Open it
steps.text: Go to http://localhost:3000. There is no sign-in and nothing to set up. You get one owner, every connector and a workspace to start in.

steps.title: Try the sample
steps.text: No data to hand? Choose Use the sample on the first page. It loads Acme Corp, a made-up software company, and walks you through the data, the goal, a ready-made ontology, its load and Ask in about a minute.

steps.title: Run a local model if you like
steps.text: This runs Ollama beside Foundry. Settings › AI models shows which model it chose and why, and lets you switch.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Click Use the sample and follow it through the Acme Corp data, the ontology and its load, then ask a question in Ask.

watch: If your shell has an Anthropic or OpenAI key set, Foundry uses that provider for AI. Ollama and LM Studio run on your own computer instead.
The local install has no sign-in. It runs as one owner with every connector turned on.
The first start writes the install's secrets into a Docker volume. `docker compose down -v` deletes that volume along with your data.
